notes: Live, full-stack AWX eval for the agentprovider skill. Unlike evals.json (offline, fixtures + `conform` oracle, CI-reproducible), this one runs end to end against a real AWX-on-Docker target with mutations and a real `terraform apply`, so it is NOT offline/CI-reproducible. It mirrors the demo / 5-round benchmark and covers all three contract kinds: author the full AWX provider surface from scratch (4 CRUD resources + 1 data source + 2 actions: an aap_job_launch and an aap_workflow_job_launch), prove each with `conform`, then apply real Terraform and execute an AWX job and a workflow job. Run it from a clean slate (no pre-existing awx_* contracts/cassettes/examples). The agent should author entirely from the skill references (0 engine-Go reads is the efficiency target). The introspect-first loop is in scope: when AWX can describe its create/update surface, run `agentprovider introspect` (read-only OPTIONS discovery) before bootstrapping each resource — note that AWX only returns the actions.POST descriptor to a write-scoped token, so a read-only token degrades introspect to source:sample/confidence:reduced.

run_config.note: Harness directive (NOT part of the task prompt the agent-under-test follows): run the eval — i.e. execute the skill under test — on CONCURRENT sonnet agents, one per contract, launched in the same turn so they author/record/conform in parallel (cost-efficient and wall-clock-fast); do skill uplift (analyzing run results/friction and rewriting SKILL.md + references) on opus. The model split keeps execution cheap while reserving the stronger model for the judgement-heavy improvement pass.
run_config.concurrency: Fan the 7 contracts out across concurrent sonnet sub-runs in one turn rather than authoring them serially. Pre-create the shared FK fixtures (one org + one inventory) and discover the read/launch fixtures (an existing job_template id, the workflow_job_template id) BEFORE fan-out, then pass those ids to the agents so each contract's record step has real parents — this removes the cross-contract ordering dependency and lets all 7 run at once. Give each created AWX object a unique name to avoid collisions between concurrent mutating records.
run_config.teardown: Cleanup is a FIRST-CLASS, VERIFIED phase of the run — not an afterthought. Mint a single unique RUN_TAG for the whole run (e.g. r<iteration>-<HHMMSS>) in setup and export it to every sub-run. EVERY AWX object the run creates — the pre-fan-out shared FK fixtures, each contract's `record --allow-mutations` objects, AND the terraform resources — MUST be named `apeval-${RUN_TAG}-*` and have its id appended to a shared teardown manifest (`<workspace>/teardown-manifest.txt`, one `kind:id` per line) as it is created. This makes teardown deterministic by tag AND by id, independent of name-matching. A run that leaves any `apeval-${RUN_TAG}-*` object behind FAILS — accumulated apeval-* objects from earlier runs are the symptom this guards against. See the `cleanup` field for the exact verified teardown procedure.
run_config.output_style: Efficiency-oriented: per-contract authoring is delegated to the concurrent sonnet sub-runs, which report concise per-command summaries + the gates that matter (conform overall_passed, the completeness/classification gate). Raw-output-on-screen is NOT required (this reverses the iteration-10 'leave raw output on screen' stance in favour of consider-efficiency).

requires: AWX reachable at $AWX (default http://localhost:30080), admin creds in $AWX_USERNAME/$AWX_PASSWORD
agentprovider CLI + terraform-provider-dynamic binary built and on PATH (demo/bin) / wired via TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE dev_overrides
a workflow job template exists in AWX for aap_workflow_job_launch to target (stock AWX/AAP ships none) — create one or point the action at an existing workflow_job_template id
setup: cd <repo root>  # MUST run from repo root: .env derives AWX_PASSWORD via a relative cat
set -a; . ./.env; set +a  # exports AWX, AWX_USERNAME, AWX_PASSWORD (persists across later cd)
agentprovider on PATH (~/.local/bin/agentprovider); terraform-provider-dynamic at repo root, wired via dev_overrides — no PATH entry needed
export TF_CLI_CONFIG_FILE=$PWD/examples/awx/dev.tfrc  # dev_overrides skips init; go straight to plan/apply
export AGENTPROVIDER_CONTRACTS=$PWD/.agentprovider/contracts  # provider CWD becomes examples/awx, so set abs contracts dir
# introspect needs a bearer token: mint one — curl -s -u "$AWX_USERNAME:$AWX_PASSWORD" -X POST $AWX/api/v2/tokens/ -d '{"scope":"write"}' — and export it as AWX_TOKEN for --auth-env

# binaries: if agentprovider lacks `introspect`, rebuild from the engine source (research-dynamic-provider) — `go build -o <dest> ./cli/agentprovider` and `go build -o <repo>/terraform-provider-dynamic .`

export RUN_TAG=r<iteration>-$(date +%H%M%S)  # single unique tag for the whole run; every created object is named apeval-${RUN_TAG}-* and id-logged to <workspace>/teardown-manifest.txt as it is created (see run_config.teardown)

# pre-clean: scan for stray apeval-*/ap-*/agentprovider* objects from EARLIER runs (org/inventory/host/job_template/workflow_job_template) and delete them — leftovers are a prior cleanup bug and cause name collisions; keep Default org id 1, Demo Project id 6, Demo * objects, and workflow_job_template id 56
oracle: All 7 contracts `conform --json` overall_passed:true (incl. the data source via read_returns_expected and both actions via action_returns_expected) AND `terraform -chdir=examples/awx apply` succeeds AND the aap_job_launch action launches a real AWX job AND the aap_workflow_job_launch action launches a real AWX workflow job (verify both via the AWX API) AND the data source reads an existing AWX object AND a second `plan` is a no-op (idempotent) AND `completeness <contract> --base-url $AWX --min-completeness 90` passes for each CRUD resource and the data source (host models `groups`; the data source models `url`/`named_url`). AWX serves no OpenAPI, so completeness uses the live response-union source. FINALLY, teardown is run and VERIFIED: `terraform destroy` + an API sweep delete every `apeval-${RUN_TAG}-*` object the run created, a post-teardown query (`name__startswith=apeval-${RUN_TAG}`) returns 0 across organizations/inventories/hosts/job_templates/workflow_job_templates, and the authored contracts/cassettes/tf-state are removed — AWX is left exactly as found (keep-fixtures untouched).

evals.name: awx-provider-from-scratch
evals.prompt: Use the agentprovider skill to build a fresh AWX provider with terraform-provider-dynamic against live AWX, then prove it with terraform apply and confirm a real AWX job launches. Use docs/awx-api-to-aap-resources.md for the Terraform type names and AWX API paths (aap_* convention); cover these 7 contracts: organization, inventory, job_template, host (Resources, full CRUD); job_template_ds (DataSource by id, exposes computed fields incl. url/named_url); job_launch and workflow_job_launch (Actions, POST .../launch/). Spawn one concurrent Sonnet 4.6 medium-effort subagent per contract (all 7 in parallel); each follows the agentprovider loop: introspect (when the API can describe its surface) → bootstrap → preflight → record --allow-mutations → conform until overall_passed → completeness gate → mutation-check/emit-proof. Creds from the sourced .env (basic auth ${env.AWX_USERNAME}/${env.AWX_PASSWORD}, base_url ${env.AWX}); never print .env, keep secrets out of all files. Output a markdown table: Resource | Kind | AWX API | conform | completeness | proven (one row per contract). Then write Terraform under examples/awx consuming the resources and wiring the job + workflow actions, run terraform apply (verify the job and workflow job via the AWX API), confirm a clean no-op second apply, and show the run logs. Print PROVEN only when all 7 conform, completeness is shown for each, apply succeeds, and the launched job + workflow job are confirmed in AWX.

assertions.text: all 7 AWX contracts conform with overall_passed:true (4 full-CRUD resources 8/8 incl. the import_reconstructs + id_stable_across_update floor; 1 data source via read_returns_expected; 2 action contracts — aap_job_launch and aap_workflow_job_launch — 1/1 each via action_returns_expected)

agentprovider introspect was run for read-only field discovery before authoring each resource (or the summary states why no live discovery path existed); against AWX this returns source:options/confidence:high only with a write-scoped token

the completeness/classification gate is shown for each resource and the data source — completeness_percent plus the settable-input classification (settable_coverage / ignored_settable) — and no settable input was parked in ignore_server_fields to inflate the number (no green-washing; the verbose job_template models its full ask_*_on_launch + behavior-toggle surface)
a data source (kind DataSource) reads an existing AWX object by id and projects at least one real computed output, proven via read_returns_expected (no create/update/delete lifecycle)
terraform apply succeeded against live AWX (org -> inventory -> host + job_template created; the data source resolved an existing object)
the aap_job_launch action executed a real AWX job (verifiable via the AWX jobs API)
the aap_workflow_job_launch action executed a real AWX workflow job via POST /api/v2/workflow_job_templates/${id}/launch/ (verifiable via the AWX workflow_jobs API)

both action contracts are action-only (kind Resource, actions block, no create lifecycle) and are wired via lifecycle { action_trigger } on a sibling resource (not the action's target, to avoid a resource->action->resource cycle)
a second terraform plan is a clean no-op (idempotent)

agentprovider completeness --base-url $AWX --min-completeness 90 passes for each CRUD resource and the data source (host models groups; data source models url/named_url) — measured against the live response-union since AWX serves no OpenAPI
no live credential values committed to any contract, cassette, or HCL (cassettes redacted; creds sourced from ${env.*})

teardown is complete and VERIFIED: `terraform destroy -auto-approve` plus an API sweep removed every object the run created (all apeval-${RUN_TAG}-* organizations/inventories/hosts/job_templates/workflow_job_templates, from both the record steps and the terraform apply), a post-teardown query for name__startswith=apeval-${RUN_TAG} returns count 0 on every endpoint, the write token minted in setup is revoked, and the authored contracts/cassettes/proofs/tf-state are removed — AWX is left as it was found, with keep-fixtures (Default org id 1, Demo * objects, workflow_job_template id 56, project id 6) untouched. Any leftover apeval-* object — from this run or a prior one — fails this assertion.

efficiency_targets.note: Targets from the 5-round benchmark: an agent should author the whole provider from the skill references alone (0 engine-Go reads), with no conform repair loops and no settings discovered at record/plan time. Baseline (pre-uplift skill) averaged ~3.3 Go-reads and 1 repair. Efficiency is now measured at the harness level too: per-contract authoring may be parallelised across sonnet sub-runs and reported as concise summaries (raw-output-on-screen is not required); skill uplift from the run is done on opus. introspect (when available) should replace blind bootstrapping of resource field shapes.

evals.cleanup: MANDATORY + VERIFIED — the run is not done until AWX is left as it was found. (1) terraform destroy first: `terraform -chdir=examples/awx destroy -auto-approve` (removes the apply graph: org/inventory/host/job_template). (2) API-sweep the record-step + fixture objects that terraform never owned: delete every object whose name starts with `apeval-${RUN_TAG}` across organizations, inventories, hosts, job_templates, workflow_job_templates, projects, credentials — prefer the teardown manifest's `kind:id` lines for exactness. Delete leaf objects before parents, OR delete the organization and let AWX cascade its inventories/job_templates. NEVER delete the keep-fixtures: Default org (id 1), Demo Project (id 6), Demo * objects, workflow_job_template id 56. (3) Revoke the write token minted in setup: `DELETE /api/v2/tokens/<id>/` (or curl the token's own delete URL). (4) VERIFY teardown — for each endpoint run `GET .../?name__startswith=apeval-${RUN_TAG}` and assert `count == 0`; if any object remains, the cleanup_complete assertion FAILS. (5) Remove authored artifacts: `rm -f .agentprovider/contracts/{organization,inventory,job_template,host,job_template_ds,job_launch,workflow_job_launch}.yaml` and their `.proven.json` sidecars and the matching `.agentprovider/cassettes/*`, then `rm -rf examples/awx/{main.tf,apply-contracts,.terraform,terraform.tfstate,terraform.tfstate.backup,dev.tfrc}`. (6) Backlog hygiene: if the pre-run scan finds stray apeval-*/ap-* objects from EARLIER runs, that is a prior cleanup bug — sweep them too (same keep-fixture exclusions) so cruft never compounds into name collisions.
